newsitem.title: ITALY: Facts and figures of World Food Summit.
newsitem.headline: Facts and figures of World Food Summit.

text.p: This week's U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit will pledge to halve the number of undernourished people worldwide from the current 840 million by the year 2015.
Following are key facts and figures about the summit, which opens on Wednesday:

* The summit is hosted by the U.N.'s Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) in its Fascist-era headquarters, which then-dictator Benito Mussolini built in 1935 to house his "Ministry for an Italian Africa". The agency moved to Rome from Washington in 1951.

* FAO says more than 100 heads of state, prime ministers or senior ministers are due to attend the five-day gathering, the largest summit aimed solely at tackling world hunger. FAO has not released a list of leaders attending for security reasons.
* More than 10,000 delegates, officials from non-governmental organisations and journalists are expected for the event. FAO says some 4,000 journalists alone are accredited.
* 10,000 police and paramilitary Carabinieri will be on duty.
* Around 170 VIPs will be staying in more than 70 hotels.

* FAO says it is doing the summit "on the cheap" and is discouraging lavish receptions to send the right signal. The gathering is expected to cost FAO, whose funding comes from its 174 member states, some $2 million in all.

* The Italian government is reported to have set aside 1.63 billion lire ($1 million) to help pay for staging the summit; it had originally budgeted 2.34 billion lire ($1.5 million) but the sum was cut after opposition from a hard-right party.
